source_text:
Epistula ad Theodosium imperatorem
̓Επιφανίου ἐπισκόπου Κύπρων Ἐπιστολὴ πρὸς Θεοδόσιον τὸν βασιλέα.
19 τὴν εἰδωλολατρείαν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τῇ ἑαυτοῦ κακοτεχνίᾳ ὁ διάβολος
ἐμηχανήσατο καὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἔσπειρε τοῦτο καὶ ἐθεμελίωσε καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους
ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπέστρεψε· νῦν δὲ πάλιν μετὰ τὰς αἱρέσεις καὶ τὰ εἴδωλα εἰς ἀρχαίαν
εἰδωλολατρείαν τοὺς πιστοὺς καθείλκυσε καὶ ἠπάτησε. 20 εἰσφέρει ἑαυτὸν ἐν τῇ
ἐπιστολῇ τῇ πίστει τῶν ἐν Νικαίᾳ πατέρων ἐκ νέας ἡλικίας ἠκολουθηκέναι καὶ ὡς οἱ
γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ἐν ταύτῃ γεγέννηνται καὶ τὴν αὐτὴν εἶχον ὁμολογίαν. 21 νοήσει γὰρ ἡ
σὴ εὐσέβεια εἰ πρέπον ἐστὶν ἔχειν ἡμᾶς θεὸν ζωγραφητὸν διὰ χρωμάτων. 22 ἤκουσα
ὡς καὶ τὸν ἀκατάληπτον υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ τινὲς γράφειν ἐπαγγέλλονται οὐ μέμνημαί τι
τοιοῦτον ἰδών.
23 Τίς τῶν παλαιῶν πατέρων Χριστοῦ εἰκόνα ζωγραφήσας ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἢ ἐν
οἴκῳ ἰδίῳ κατέθετο ἢ ἐν βήλοις θυρῶν;
thought_title: The devil's trick and the question of painted images
orientation: Epiphanius opens his letter to the emperor by describing how the devil introduced idolatry and now deceives believers, then begins questioning whether any ancient father painted an image of Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Letter to the emperor Theodosius. Of Epiphanius bishop of Cyprus a letter to Theodosius the emperor. The devil contrived idolatry in the world by his own evil art and sowed this in the world and established it and turned humans away from God; but now again after the heresies and the idols he dragged down the faithful into ancient idolatry and deceived them. He brings himself in the letter to have followed the faith of the fathers in Nicaea from young age and that his parents were born in this and had the same confession. For your piety will understand whether it is fitting for us to have a painted God through colors. I heard that some also promise to paint the incomprehensible Son of God; I do not remember having seen any such thing. Which of the old fathers painted an image of Christ and placed it in a church or in his own house or on curtains of doors?

choices.why: Glossary term; renders the worship of images as gods without the banned 'image-worship'
Glossary term; keeps the literal sense of depiction with colors
Glossary term 'curtains' for βῆλα; literal genitive 'of doors' preserved
Literal force of pulling down into idolatry, matching the verb's physical sense
Standard theological sense of what cannot be grasped or contained

pass_b_english: The devil contrived idolatry in the world by his own evil art, sowed it in the world and established it, and turned human beings away from God. Now again, after the heresies and the idols, he has dragged the faithful down into the ancient idolatry and deceived them. Epiphanius brings himself forward in the letter as having followed the faith of the fathers at Nicaea from his youth, and as having parents who were born in that faith and held the same confession. For your piety will understand whether it is fitting for us to have a painted God made with colors. I have heard that some even promise to paint the incomprehensible Son of God; I do not recall ever seeing such a thing.
Which of the ancient fathers painted an image of Christ and set it up in a church or in his own house, or on the curtains of doors?
